subject: spike and slab prior for spatial-specific coefficients

messages.author: b7aa09b7deb1f038
messages.subject: spike and slab prior for spatial-specific coefficients
parts:
Dear,

I am trying to assign a spike and slab prior for spatial-specific coefficients, but it doesn't work with the indicator parameters do not iterate (the modes are the same as the initial values given). 
I have tried standard linear model with spike and slab prior, it works well. However, I don't know why it cannot work with spatial-specific coefficients.
Here are some simulated data:

i) standard linear model:

S <- 159   # number of locations
X <- rmvnorm(159, sigma = diag(rep(1, 6)))
b <- c(-1, 2, 0, 0, 2, 1)
y <- as.vector(2 + bm0 %*% t(X[,]) + rnorm(S))

nimbleCode({
  for (i in 1:S) {
    y[i] ~ dnorm(mu_y[i], tau = tau_y)
    
    mu_y[i] <- b0 + b[1] * x1[i] + b[2] * x2[i] + b[3] * x3[i] + b[4] * x4[i] + 
      b[5] * x5[i] + b[6] * x6[i]
  }
  
  for (j in 1:6) {
    b[j] ~ dnorm(mu_bm[j], tau_bm[j])
    mu_bm[j] <- 0
    tau_bm[j] <- tau_bmm[ind[j] + 1]
    ind[j] ~ dbern(gamma[j])
    gamma[j] ~ dbeta(0.5, 0.5)
  }
  
  tau_bmm[1] <- tau_b0      # tau_b0 = 100, c = 0.0001
  tau_bmm[2] <- tau_b0 * c
  
  
  b0 ~ dnorm(0, 1)
  tau_y ~ dgamma(1, 1)
})

It works well. 

ii) spatial-specific coefficients:

S <- 159   # number of locations
X <- rmvnorm(159, sigma = diag(rep(1, 6)))
b1 <- rep(-1, S) + rnorm(S)
b2 <- rep(2, S) + rnorm(S)
b3 <- rep(0, S)
b4 <- rep(0, S)
b5 <- rep(2, S) + rnorm(S)
b6 <- rep(1, S) + rnorm(S)
y <- 1 + b1 * X[, 1] + b2 * X[, 2] + b3 * X[, 3] + b4 * X[, 4] + b5 * X[, 5] + b6 * X[, 6] + rnorm(S) 

nimbleCode({
  for (i in 1:S) {
    y[i] ~ dnorm(mu_y[i], tau = tau_y)
    mu_y[i] <- b0 + b[i, 1] * x1[i] + b[i, 2] * x2[i] +
      b[i, 3] * x3[i] + b[i, 4] * x4[i] + b[i, 5] * x5[i] +
      b[i, 6] * x6[i]
    
    b[i, 1:6] ~ dmnorm(mu_bm[1:6], cov = var_bm[1:6, 1:6])
  }
  
  
  var_bm[1:6, 1:6] <- diag(1/tau_bm[1:6])
  
  for (j in 1:6) {
    mu_bm[j] <- 0
    tau_bm[j] <- tau_bmm[ind[j] + 1]
    ind[j] ~ dbern(gamma[j])
    gamma[j] ~ dbeta(0.5, 0.5)
  }
  
  tau_bmm[1] <- tau_b0
  tau_bmm[2] <- tau_b0 * c
  
  b0 ~ dnorm(0, 1)
  tau_y ~ dgamma(1, 1)
  
})

Cannot iterate for parameter "ind".


Could you help me with that?



Best,
Zhihua

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: spike and slab prior for spatial-specific coefficients
parts:
Zhihua, thanks for your usage of NIMBLE.  Unfortunately, I'm not able to re-create the error you mentioned ("Cannot iterate for parameter "ind")

I'm including my code below, slightly modified from your original, which runs fine for me, and the mixing / sampling appears to get off to a fine start (although I only ran it for 10,000 iterations).  The changes I made include:

-- Adding initial values for the b[1:159, 1:6] array, so that your model is fully initialized.
-- Changing from using nimbleMCMC(), to using the more modular and configurable workflow of using nimbleModel(), then configureMCMC(), buildMCMC(), and runMCMC().
-- Running for fewer iterations, and I skipped the thinning of the samples, but you can add that back in.

Anyway, it runs fine for me.  Please give this a try, and let us know if you still are having problems.

Which version of NIMBLE are you using?  It could perhaps be, that in older versions of NIMBLE, the dynamic indexing that you're using (with the "ind" variable) either wasn't implemented, or was "turned off" by default.  So you might consider trying to upgrade to NIMBLE version 0.7.2 available on CRAN.

Good luck!

Daniel

library(nimble)
library(mvtnorm)

S <- 159   # number of locations
X <- rmvnorm(159, sigma = diag(rep(1, 6)))
b1 <- rep(-1, S) + rnorm(S)
b2 <- rep(2, S) + rnorm(S)
b3 <- rep(0, S)
b4 <- rep(0, S)
b5 <- rep(2, S) + rnorm(S)
b6 <- rep(1, S) + rnorm(S)
y <- 1 + b1 * X[, 1] + b2 * X[, 2] + b3 * X[, 3] + b4 * X[, 4] + b5 * X[, 5] + b6 * X[, 6] + rnorm(S)

##(ii) spatial-specific coefficients
code <- nimbleCode({

for (i in 1:S) {
        y[i] ~ dnorm(mu_y[i], tau = tau_y)
        mu_y[i] <-
            b0 + b[i, 1] * x1[i] + b[i, 2] * x2[i] +
            b[i, 3] * x3[i] + b[i, 4] * x4[i] + b[i, 5] * x5[i] + b[i, 6] * x6[i]
        b[i, 1:6] ~ dmnorm(mu_bm[1:6], cov = var_bm[1:6, 1:6])
    }
    var_bm[1:6, 1:6] <- diag(1/tau_bm[1:6])
    for (j in 1:6) {
        mu_bm[j] <- 0
        tau_bm[j] <- tau_bmm[ind[j] + 1]
        ind[j] ~ dbern(gamma[j])
        gamma[j] ~ dbeta(0.5, 0.5)
    }
    tau_bmm[1] <- tau_b0
    tau_bmm[2] <- tau_b0 * c
    b0 ~ dnorm(0, 1)
    tau_y ~ dgamma(1, 1)
})
constants <- list(S = 159, c = 0.0001, tau_b0 = 100)
data <- list(y = y, x1 = X[,1], x2 = X[,2], x3 =X[,3], x4 = X[,4], x5 = X[,5], x6 = X[,6])

inits <- list(tau_y = 1, tau_bm = rep(1,6), b0 = rnorm(1), ind = rep(1,6), gamma = runif(6),
              b = array(0, c(159,6)))   ## DT: added initial value for b array

Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code, constants, data, inits)

## DT: calculate() returns a real number, model is fully initialized
Rmodel$calculate()   

conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel)

## check the sampler assignments.
## might consider whether or not you want the RW_block samplers assigned
## to each b[i, 1:6] ?
conf$printSamplers()

## add your monitors
conf$addMonitors(c("b0","b","ind","gamma","tau_y"))

Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)

Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)

set.seed(0)
samples <- runMCMC(Cmcmc, 10000)

samplesSummary(samples)

library(basicMCMCplots)
samplesPlot(samples, c('gamma', 'b0'))

##mcmc.out <- nimbleMCMC(code, constants, data, inits,
##                       monitors = c("b0","b","ind","gamma","tau_y"),
##                       niter = 50000, thin = 10, nchains = 1, setSeed = TRUE)

SConsts <- list(S = 159, c = 0.0001, tau_b0 = 100)
SInits <- list(tau_y = 1,
                  tau_bm = rep(1, 6),
                  b0 = rnorm(1),
                  ind = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1),
                  gamma = runif(6)

mcmc.out <- nimbleMCMC(code = SCode, data = Sdata, constants = SConsts,
                       inits = SInits,
                       monitors = c("b0","b"
                                    ,"ind","gamma"
                                    ,"tau_y"
                       ),

                       thin = 10, nchains = 1, setSeed = TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: spike and slab prior for spatial-specific coefficients
parts:
Hi Zhihua,

We've taken a more thorough look at this. The nimble code seems to be working as it should, but it looks like this model is not likely to mix much. As the model is written, in order to have a change in the status of an indicator variable, e.g. say from ind[3] = 0 (slab) to 1 (spike), all the corresponding  parameters b[, 3] should be *simultaneously* close to zero, which will be very rare.  Conversely, a move from the spike to the slab would be very unlikely because if all of the b[,3] parameters are close to zero, then the spike will have much higher probability than the slab.

We've more often seen spike and slab priors written with indicator variables that multiply coefficients, rather than modifying the variance (or precision) of the prior for the coefficients.  For example, one might write something like:

b0 + ind[1]*b[i, 1] * x1[i] + ... (similar for other coefficients).

So if an indicator variable is equal to zero, it also sets to zero the associated vector of coefficients; otherwise coefficients follow the slab distribution. Then the prior on the indicator variables' probability of being 1 is the probability of being in the slab.

Another approach would be to write custom samplers that could mix the indicator variables and coefficients jointly.  The "examples" tab at r-nimble.org shows an example with a reversible-jump sampler for a similar kind of problem. (We are working to make this more flexible and include it in nimble). See also Section 15.5 of the user manual which documents writing new samplers. 

Best,

Sally

Zhihua, thanks for your usage of NIMBLE.  Unfortunately, I'm not able to re-create the error you mentioned ("Cannot iterate for parameter "ind")

I'm including my code below, slightly modified from your original, which runs fine for me, and the mixing / sampling appears to get off to a fine start (although I only ran it for 10,000 iterations).  The changes I made include:

-- Adding initial values for the b[1:159, 1:6] array, so that your model is fully initialized.
-- Changing from using nimbleMCMC(), to using the more modular and configurable workflow of using nimbleModel(), then configureMCMC(), buildMCMC(), and runMCMC().
-- Running for fewer iterations, and I skipped the thinning of the samples, but you can add that back in.

Anyway, it runs fine for me.  Please give this a try, and let us know if you still are having problems.

Which version of NIMBLE are you using?  It could perhaps be, that in older versions of NIMBLE, the dynamic indexing that you're using (with the "ind" variable) either wasn't implemented, or was "turned off" by default.  So you might consider trying to upgrade to NIMBLE version 0.7.2 available on CRAN.

Good luck!

Daniel
